title: Structured interview rubric pilot results
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the outcomes from the 3-week pilot of a structured interview rubric for backend/platform engineer candidates (mid-senior levels). Goal was to test whether a more explicit rubric improves inter-rater reliability, speeds debriefs, and reduces unconscious bias signals in decisions.

Pilot scope and timeline:
- Dates: 2025-04-07 -> 2025-04-25
- Roles: Backend / Serving Runtime / Platform-engineering ICs (L4-L6 hiring funnel)
- Interviewers: Miguel, Tanya, Noah, Priya, Leah + rotating panel of 10 interviewers across teams
- Candidates interviewed under pilot rubric: 18 (mix of internal referrals, recruiter-sourced, and campus pipeline)

Rubric overview used in pilot (what we asked interviewers to score):
- Core technical (algorithms/data structures + code correctness) — weight 40
- System design (scalability, tradeoffs, operational concerns) — weight 30
- Communication & collaboration (clarity, feedback loop, pair-programming style) — weight 20
- Role fit / ops awareness (monitoring, debugging, infra empathy) — weight 10
Scoring scale: 1 (poor) to 5 (exceptional). Guidance doc included examples and anchors for 1/3/5.

High level outcomes:
- Distribution of pass recommendations (panel hire vs no-hire): 6 strong hire, 5 hire-with-concerns, 4 borderline (ask for second interview), 3 reject.
- Average time to debrief per interview dropped from ~17m (previous average) to ~11m when panel used rubric anchors — we tracked 31 debriefs in the window.
- Inter-rater variance: still material. Technical scores had higher agreement (intra-class correlation ~0.62) than system design (0.48) and role fit (0.35).
- Observed bias signposts: female candidates scored similarly on technical but slightly lower on role-fit; small N but flagged for monitoring.

What went well:
- Faster alignment in debriefs: the score cards gave starting points and reduced long monologues in post-interview syncs.
- Less post-hoc justification: panels referenced rubric anchors (e.g., "candidate did X -> 3/5 on design because lacked explicit load discussion").
- Easier note aggregation: recruiter and hiring managers appreciated structured fields for passing to ATS.

Pain points / anomalies:
- Anchors still too high-level for design interviews. Interviewers wanted more concrete prompts/checklist (e.g., ask about dataflow, state management, KV caching patterns).
- Some interviewers treated the rubric rigidly; others used it as a loose guide. Need training to reduce variability in application.
- Role-fit category conflates product curiosity and operational habits — those are distinct signals but were being merged.
- Small sample size for equity analyses; flagged as "monitor and expand" not definitive.

Recommendations (short term):
1) Update rubric doc to split role-fit into two separate subcategories: "ops empathy" and "product/problem framing" (owner: Tanya Li, due 2025-05-08).
2) Add 6 concrete anchor examples for the system-design rubric (owner: Miguel Rivera, due 2025-05-06). These should include brief prompts for latency/backpressure, caching, and deployment/rollback considerations.
3) Run a mandatory 45-minute calibration session for active interviewers before next hiring batch. Focus: using anchors, avoiding narrative drift (owner: Noah Kim, schedule by 2025-05-05).
4) Instrument debrief forms in Greenhouse/ATS to capture the 4 numeric scores plus a 1-line "primary risk" field (owner: Recruiting ops, linked ticket HH-4823).
5) Expand pilot to 50 interviews over next 8 weeks to get better metrics for fairness checks (owner: Priya Singh, plan due 2025-05-12).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Should we weight system design higher for L5+ candidates? Proposal: for L5+, design weight -> 35, technical -> 35, communication -> 20, ops -> 10. Need hiring leads sign-off. (Action: Leah to collect lead opinions by 2025-05-09).
- How to reliably capture interviewer training completion? We have a 1-pager but not enforcement. Suggest adding a short quiz in LMS. (Action: People Ops + Eng Dev to scoping doc by 2025-05-15).

Calibration notes from debriefs (direct excerpts):
- "Candidate A: good DS fundamentals, but didn't discuss eviction/backpressure on the stateful path -> we marked 3/5 on design." (Miguel)
- "Candidate F: concise communicator but avoided operational tradeoffs; we disagreed whether that's a coaching gap or a product-sense miss." (Tanya)
- "Panel tends to default to technical when unclear; we need explicit rule when scores conflict (e.g., median vs weighted average)." (Noah)

Action item tracker (short):
- Tanya Li: update rubric doc with split role-fit and doc examples — due 2025-05-08.
- Miguel Rivera: craft 6 system-design anchors, add to doc and slide deck — due 2025-05-06.
- Noah Kim: schedule and run calibration session; create sample debrief role-play — complete by 2025-05-05.
- Priya Singh (recruiting): expand pilot plan to 50 interviews and coordinate with sourcers — plan due 2025-05-12.
- Leah O'Connor: collect hiring lead weight preferences and synthesize recommendations — due 2025-05-09.
- Recruiting ops: instrument numeric fields in ATS (HH-4823) — implement in next sprint.

Risks/Dependences:
- Running a larger pilot depends on recruiter bandwidth and open reqs — Priya flagged potential capacity hit in week of 2025-05-19.
- Calibration effectiveness depends on interviewer attendance; suggest linking completion to interview rotation signup.

Next steps for meeting coming 2025-05-07:
- Quick review of updated rubric (Tanya/Miguel)
- Decision on L5 weight change (Leah to present aggregated lead opinions)
- Agree go/no-go to expand pilot to 50 interviews

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a "mini case" for system-design that is 20m long and calibrated across interviewers — reduces variation in problem selection.
- Potentially pair new interviewers with an experienced interviewer for first 3 debriefs (mentorship loop).
- Add a one-line diversity/fairness checklist to interviewer guidance (avoid questions that privilege prior access to specific systems).

If you have immediate feedback or want a slot on the calibration session, ping me or drop a note in slack #eng-hiring.

Document history / provenance:
- Drafted by Asha Patel 2025-04-29 after pilot closeout compendium.
- Added calibration action items and small edits 2025-05-01 (Tanya/Miguel comments).
- Last modified 2025-05-02 (Noah added session logistics).
